process_steps.output_state: supersaturated solid solution of pre-alloyed oxygen-containing powders

evidence.quote: The powders were mechanically alloyed using dry ball milling under an air atmosphere for 40 h, with a ball-to-powder weight ratio of 4:1 (tungsten carbide grinding balls) and a rotation speed of 280 r/min.

The alloyed powders were consolidated by SPS under a vacuum of < 5 Pa and an axial pressure of 30 MPa. The temperature was ramped at 80 °C/min to 1050 °C, held for 8 min, resulting in bulk samples with a diameter of 50 mm and a thickness of 8 mm.

These precipitates can significantly strengthen the material by impeding dislocation movement [10] , enhancing hetero-deformation induced hardening [7] , and promoting the formation of protective oxide layers during high-temperature sliding [9 , 20] .
The coupled precipitates promote tribo-oxidation and subsurface recrystallization, forming a dense (Cr, Nb)-rich tribo-oxide layer that enhances surface stiffness and suppress damage accumulation.
The high yield strength primarily stems from precipitation strengthening, solid solution hardening, and lattice distortion effects.
